106: # In particular, if an untrusted app links to other app data
107: # files, installd will not be able to guarantee the deletion
108: # of the linked to file. Hard links also contribute to security
109: # bugs, so we want to ensure untrusted apps never have this
110: # capability.

platform_interpretation: Android15 AOSP explicitly neverallows untrusted app domains from hard-linking any file_type:file (app_neverallows.te105-111), including app_data_file. The runtime AVC identifies this very untrusted_app/app_data_file/link boundary with Enforcing behavior.

Ordinary app sandbox file creation permission uses create_file_perms, which omits link. Moving from cacheDir to filesDir/codeCacheDir or using another Java/native link wrapper is not a justified fix for the missing SELinux operation.

The public android-15.0.0_r1 policy is cited as source context; this review did not extract or compare the exact compiled policy of image fingerprint Android/sdk_phone64_x86_64/emu64x:15/AE3A.240806.019/12368160:userdebug/test-keys.
No chmod/chcon, SELinux override, privileged setup, run-as/shell substitution, assumption-based skip or fake inode is proposed as a passing hardlink test.

future_os_bind_alias_proposal.status: Source-backed candidate only; neither implemented nor exercised. Not a hardlink equivalent or replacement.
future_os_bind_alias_proposal.platform_basis: AOSP init.rc991-995 documents OS binding /data/data onto /data/user/0, without requiring the app to create any hard link or mount.
preconditions: Use only this test app's own random cache file and the corresponding user0 /data/data versus /data/user/0 path; do not guess another app/profile path.

Require both paths to exist and be regular files, different serialized URIs and different canonicalFile values, and real nonzero identical Os.stat dev+inode BEFORE invoking the library. Any inaccessible path, unified canonical path or mismatch is a failed/unavailable candidate, not a skip/pass.
Require the normal same-file saver outcome to preserve both paths and bytes, then verify native descriptor cleanup. Keep the existing distinct-inode positive copy control.
App data-isolation mounts or nonzero-user/OEM storage topology may change accessibility; do not label this portable until actually verified on the target.
